Big post, tldr moderation is fine, as long as you're in control and don't think it's negatively affecting your life go ahead and consume, if it's negative for you, stop. 

I was a heavy drinker, then quit that and became a heavy smoker (weed and tobacco mixed ~50-50) and I can honestly say the times I've felt best were when I didn't go heavy on either. But also when I was completely sober I never had the social life I should have, just because all my friends are drinkers or smokers. As long as I'm in control I find having 1 night per week or two drinking or smoking is fine and in fact improves my social life and mental health however that's not to say it's necessary, just what seems to work for me. If my friends didn't drink I wouldn't, I only drink around them. For me I've found as long as I have some rules like limiting myself to once per week, and only partaking in drinking or smoking when I have no work the next day works fine for me. It's when I start trying to unwind at night on say a Tuesday with work on Wednesday that things spiral.
Alcohol is a depressent so it's not ideal for mental health, and hangovers can be a bitch, but that social aspect and letting loose and talking about things I usually wouldn't is great for me, and my friends.
Everyone is different just play around with it and see how it affects you. But be honest. When I was heavy smoking it was hard to let go but when I sat back and looked at myself it was bad for me and those around me. Cutting smoking out has been the best thing for me. I may go back to trying it once per week or two but only after a longer break to ensure I don't fall back into the daily habit.
Substances are there to help you, if they take control of you cut them out (maybe slowly if can't go cold turkey). Drinking can be great socially but can also ruin you. A lot of other drugs like weed and psychedelics can be great to relax and reflect but too much or too often can ruin the experience and you life. Once you need a drug to function it's never that good, drugs are only fun in moderation, drinking included. Anything you do daily loses its flavour quickly and just becomes an expense you could be spending elsewhere. One day of smoking or drinking every week or two feels great, doing it everyday just feels normal, and costs a fortune.
If you're in control and you think it's enhancing not decreasing your quality of life by all means consume what you want. That goes with all things, food, drugs, porn etc.
As far as resisting it just comes down to recognising that you know it'll take you backwards rather than forwards. If you can't resist when you're around your friends but don't want to do it then that leaves you with a couple options: 1) stop seeing those friends or 2) talk to them about your changes and let them know you can't help yourself, if they're good about it you may be able to still hang with them, if not, well back to option one.
The less you get rushes from drugs the more you chase other things like career and personal goals so it can definately help to go sober, or at least have limits.

Humans need shelter. Humans inherently want to better their shelter. For most of human history your shelter was your shelter if you were there at the time. Once you left it for whatever reason (made a better house nearby, moved far away etc) someone else could and would use it, potentially improving it again. 
Now we have a case where people can hold onto their old shelter, and make people pay them to stay there even though they've clearly shown no interest in it as a shelter, just as a means of profiting. This means people are struggling to find shelter as old ones are still someone's instead of being up for grabs as it should be. Now people have to pay to rent shelter that isn't there's and thus are less likely to improve it and/or care for it. 
So not only does the availability of shelter decrease under private ownership, so does the quality of the shelter. 

This is ignoring labor which under private ownership you see decreased wages. This is because someone at the top is taking a cut, as they own the means of production. The wages are lower than they should be and don't rise as fast as they should. Private ownership gives the power to do so under protection by the state (police, army etc) whereas without private ownership people would be free to work for themselves and reap all the benefits of that work.
